title: A water barometer (পানির ব্যারোমিটার)
placement: Book page 145, topic 5.4.1 (টরিসেলির পরীক্ষা): beside the paragraph on the 10.3 m of cold drink ('কোল্ড ড্রিংকসটা 10.3 মিটার পর্যন্ত উঠে হঠাৎ করে থেমে গেছে') and the 13.6 times denser mercury.
description: A water barometer (page 145, topic 5.4.1) as one guided sequence with one big step button and one short Bangla line per step, on a round teak platform under a calm evening-blue backdrop. (1) The mercury barometer as in a clean textbook drawing: a glass tube closed at the top standing in a dish, the silver mercury column at 76 cm, the vacuum (শূন্যতা) above it, an outlined blue air-pressure arrow on the dish and an orange 76 cm dimension line. (2) 'What if water, not mercury?': the same tube and dish, 11 m tall, with lightly tinted blue water, appear beside it; the camera pulls back smoothly while the water rises and stops at 10.3 m with a vacuum above, beside a 0–11 m measuring staff and a 1.6 m student for the scale (about six people tall); the mercury barometer stays at the foot, tiny, with an equal air-pressure arrow. (3) Compare: 13.6 orange pieces of 76 cm stack up beside the water's column, one beside the mercury; the panel gives the book's reason (mercury is 13.6 times as dense as water: 76 cm × 13.6 ≈ 10.3 m). (4) The book's straw: the tube becomes a 10.5 m straw of cold drink, the camera rises to its top, and the drink stops at 10.3 m with the top 0.2 m empty, however hard you suck. 'আবার দেখো' starts over. The tubes are drawn thicker than real ones (said in the panel). Test tab: 4 questions (how tall a water column, why so tall, what is above it, a 12 m straw), every wrong choice with its own note. Split from torricelli-barometer. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
